summary.headline: Lloyds Metals Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 498% YoY to INR1,679 crore at a 33.73% margin; FY27 iron ore guidance is 26 million tons.
summary.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter on record, with total income of INR4,977 crore (up 310% YoY), EBITDA of INR1,679 crore and PAT of INR1,066 crore. For FY26, iron ore volumes rose 120% to 21.96 million tons and standalone EBITDA margin was 33.77%, which management attributes to pellets, the slurry pipeline and operating leverage. Management guided FY27 to 26 million tons of iron ore, 7.75-8 million tons of pellets and a steel wire rod start, and presented copper and cobalt expansion in Congo through Surya and CHEMAF. Consolidated capex plans rise sharply, with about INR15,000 crore planned for FY27 including copper, and debt funding is planned at 1-1.5x EBITDA.

segments.name: Iron ore (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 production 9.09 million tons (+529% YoY) and sales 6.16 million tons (+271% YoY); FY26 sales 16.18 million tons (+71%). Realisation INR5,848/t in Q4 and INR5,806/t for FY26; EBITDA/t INR1,894 in Q4 and INR1,930 for FY26. April 2026 run rate about 2 million tons per month.

segments.name: Pellets
segments.commentary: Q4 production 1.08 million tons; FY26 3.03 million tons. Q4 realisation INR9,590/t and EBITDA INR4,040/t. Second 2 million-ton-plus plant commissioned May 2026, taking capacity to 8 million tons per annum.

segments.name: DRI and power
segments.commentary: Q4 DRI sales 188,000 tons (+171% YoY); FY26 480,000 tons (+56%). Q4 DRI realisation INR27,306/t and EBITDA INR7,999/t. Power volumes up 48% YoY in Q4.

segments.name: Value-added products
segments.commentary: VAP share of FY26 standalone revenue 32% (from 20% in FY25) and of EBIT 30% (from 11%).

segments.name: Thriveni (coal and iron ore mining)
segments.commentary: FY26 EBITDA INR1,990 crore, margin about 25%. FY27 iron ore volumes in Odisha guided to 34-35 million tons (+39%); Gadchiroli volume growth guided above 75% including BHQ. Coal production 17.5 million tons in FY26.

segments.name: Copper (Surya, Congo)
segments.commentary: Surya copper plant (12,000 tpa cathode) commissioned March 2026; about 700-750 tons produced to date, running at 40-45 tons/day. FY26 copper guided at 9,000-10,000 tons per management's sentence.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone guidance: iron ore production 26 million tons, dispatches 27 million tons, pellets 7.75-8 million tons, DRI 825,000 tons, and wire rod production about 150,000 tons from the new steel plant.
Management said FY28 steel plant would run at about 1 million tons (75-80% of capacity) and pellets at 8-9 million tons.
Annual cost savings above INR2,000 crore expected, with logistics and sustainability initiatives maturing by March 2028.
Thriveni FY27 volume growth expected above 75% including BHQ; Odisha iron ore volume 34-35 million tons.
Thriveni FY27 EBITDA contribution from Geomysore gold MDO targeted at about INR60 crore.
Copper: Chemaf expected to produce meaningfully from July 2027; about 90,000 tons of copper targeted over 3-5 years across Chemaf and Surya; 30,000 tpa expansion pathway at Surya.

Capex: standalone INR10,000-11,000 crore in FY27 and INR12,500 crore-plus in FY28 per management; consolidated FY27 capex about INR15,000 crore including copper (about USD200-260 million) and Thriveni (about INR1,000 crore).
capex_capacity: Capex of about INR13,500 crore over FY24-FY26; FY26 standalone capex about INR8,100 crore. INR5,100 crore capitalised (mainly pellet plant 1, slurry pipeline, DRI); INR1,850 crore capital advances; balance CWIP.
Pellet capacity 8 million tons per annum after pellet plant 2 (May 2026); management targets about 10 million tons after debottlenecking, pending government approvals expected by FY27 year-end.
BHQ beneficiation first phase targeted for December 2027: 30 million tons input and about 12 million tons output; main equipment ordered from a European supplier.
Steel plant (blast furnace, arc furnace, coke oven, 1.2 million tpa wire rod mill) at Chandrapur in final commissioning stage, expected in Q4 FY27.
Hedri to Ghugus 195 km pipeline in advanced planning; expected to cut logistics cost by more than INR500/t for most iron ore output.

Chemaf plant capex initially about USD1.1 billion, over USD800 million spent; further USD200-260 million needed; plants 85-90% complete; Chemaf debt about USD800 million, of which USD475 million to be reduced via creditor settlements and about USD330 million non-recourse; further USD200 million asset-level borrowing planned.
demand_pricing: Management said iron ore pricing is driven by the market and Lloyds is in line with the rest of the market; steel demand described as strong, especially in India.
Pellet realisation fell sequentially as volumes rose: the company searched for new, more distant markets, lost some earlier tenders and increased exports.
Pricing parity with competition maintained while volume rose 120%.
Captive consumption of about 9 million tons of iron ore in FY27 (about 8.8 million for pellets and 0.2 million for DRI).

Receivables on consolidated basis rose to INR1,480 crore from INR171 crore; management said Thriveni was consolidated for only nine months and the company has no clear explanation yet and will revert.
Thriveni receivables cited at 15-30 days; Tata Steel slurry pipeline arrangement is take-or-pay with no exclusivity for other buyers.

qa_highlights.question: Economics of the Tata Steel slurry pipeline arrangement and whether other steel players can be served.
qa_highlights.answer: Management described it as a take-or-pay contract with low sustaining capex, with the entire capacity dedicated to Tata Steel near Kalinganagar. Rajesh Gupta said there is no exclusivity.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated FY27-FY28 capex, sustainable leverage and deleveraging plans.
qa_highlights.answer: Riyaz Shaikh said about INR14,500 crore remains to be spent over two years, with standalone FY27 at INR10,000-11,000 crore and FY28 at INR12,500 crore-plus. Consolidated FY27 is about INR15,000 crore including copper. Debt is to be raised at 1-1.5x EBITDA, with no equity planned; Thriveni RPS of about INR700 crore was paid in April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Ramp-up and revenue contribution from Congo copper and cobalt assets.
qa_highlights.answer: Surya is producing copper cathode at 40-45 tons/day, with 9,000-10,000 tons expected in FY27 per management. Chemaf will not produce this year and is expected to reach about 90,000 tons from July 2027, with sulfuric acid supply being solved in the next three months.

qa_highlights.question: Pellet capacity utilisation and target with two plants.
qa_highlights.answer: Rajesh Gupta said the first plant did 3 million tons in its first nine months, and the company targets 7.5-8 million tons in FY27 across both plants, with 10 million tons as a target after debottlenecking but no guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated receivables increase from INR171 crore to INR1,480 crore.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the comparison is not like-for-like since Thriveni was consolidated for only nine months, and no clear reason was given for the movement; the company will revert.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the government iron ore ASP and royalty rules on BHQ economics.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said royalties at 50% for material below 45% grade and 75% below 35% reduce BHQ input cost, with cost upside of INR200-300/t and selling or internal usage upside of INR700-800/t for BHQ product at 66-67% grade.

financial_highlights.change: +498% YoY; margin up more than 1,000 bps YoY

financial_highlights.value: Total income INR7,997 crore; EBITDA INR1,990 crore; margin approx. 25%; cash PAT INR1,196 crore
financial_highlights.change: Q4 EBITDA INR910 crore at 36% margin; FY25 EBITDA INR1,062 crore

risks_watch: Consolidated receivables rose to INR1,480 crore from INR171 crore; management has no clear explanation yet and promised to revert, so verify the reason and the working-capital days.

Chemaf ramp-up depends on sulfuric acid supply (expected to be solved within about three months) and on plants being completed; Chemaf produces nothing in FY27 and meaningful output is guided only from July 2027.

Funding need: about INR15,000 crore consolidated capex in FY27 with debt at 1-1.5x EBITDA and no equity planned; watch leverage and Chemaf's roughly USD330 million non-recourse debt plus a further USD200 million asset-level borrowing.
Pellet realisation fell sequentially as volumes rose and new, more distant markets were sought; watch whether pricing holds as the second 2 million-ton plant ramps.

Government iron ore ASP and royalty rules: management cited royalty rates of 50% and 75% for low-grade material and BHQ upside of INR200-300/t cost and INR700-800/t realisation, but BHQ first phase is not until December 2027.
Pending government approvals for pellet debottlenecking to about 10 million tons, expected by FY27 year-end; no formal guidance given.
Congo operations carry geopolitical and operating risk; management cited US critical-minerals backing, but Panguna (Bougainville) remains at discussion stage with no asset acquired.
key_quotes: The EBITDA margin has held steady at approximately 34% across both the last 2 quarters, demonstrating structural cost efficiency and not one-off gains.
Chemaf will not produce anything this year. It is expected to start production meaningfully by July of 2027 when the plants are expected to be commissioned.
We don't have a clear cut answer on why exactly that movement is there. We'll come back very shortly on that.
Equity as of now, we've not planned of anything and we don't -- in near future, so we don't intend on that.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations, pellet ramp-up, margins and copper timelines, but noticeably evasive on several questions: consolidated receivables, the intra-group captive transfer figure, the revenue and EBITDA bridge for FY27, and the exact Congo capex, where management said numbers were still being worked out. Management repeatedly deferred to "we will come back" on open items.
